title: Japanese-Style Vegan Burgers
subtitle: with Miso Mayo and Sweet Potato Wedges
description: Stop the flavour bus! Here's a brand-new recipe from our culinary dream team. Like all our dishes, it's got five easy cooking steps plus tips and hacks to make it your own. We think it’s a total winner – but you tell us! Leave a rating and comment through your account to let us know your thoughts.

steps.text: Roast sweet potato: Preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Cut the sweet potatoes into 2cm-thick wedges. Put the sweet potato on the lined tray, drizzle with 2 tsp vegetable oil, season with salt and pepper and toss to coat. Roast on the upper oven shelf for 20-25 mins until golden and tender.

Make slaw: Meanwhile, thinly slice the cabbage with a sharp knife or mandoline. Put the sesame seeds, 2 tsp soy sauce, 2 tsp white vinegar and ½ tsp sugar in a large bowl and stir to combine. Add the cabbage and toss to combine. Taste, then season with pepper.
Cook plant-based patties: Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in a medium frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the plant-based patties for 4-5 mins each side until browned. Remove the pan from the heat.
Toast bread rolls: While the patties are cooking, cut the bread rolls in half. Put on an oven tray, cut side up, and bake on the lower shelf for 5-6 mins until lightly toasted.

Make miso mayo and serve: Combine half the miso and 2 tbs vegan mayonnaise in a bowl. Spread the bread roll bases with the miso mayo. Layer the bases with half the slaw and the plant-based patties, then sandwich with the tops. Serve with the sweet potato wedges and remaining slaw. Enjoy!

Did you know?: You've probably heard of miso soup, but miso can be used in so many other ways – in marinades, dressings and even desserts. Miso is a thick paste made from fermented soybeans, it has a salty, rich flavour and brings lots of umami to a dish. And because it's a fermented food, it's good for you too.
